bio: Pablo Lavigne, an economist trained at UCA with a master's and doctorate from Universidad del CEMA, has been Secretary of Production Coordination in the Ministry of Economy since December 2024. Under Mauricio Macri he directed foreign-trade facilitation and ran the single foreign-trade window (VUCEA). He earlier led the Secretariat of Industry and Commerce, driving import deregulation, courier-limit increases and tariff cuts. After the Industry & Commerce secretariat fell vacant, a March 2026 decree merged those functions into his secretariat, which he now exercises on an acting basis.

Brazilian engineer and telecom executive with more than 26 years in the telecommunications/IT sector, including some 21 years at operator Oi in operations, planning, regulatory and commercial roles. From 2023 to 2025 he led state-owned Telebras. President Lula named him Minister of Communications in April 2025, with the handover ceremony in early May 2025, succeeding Juscelino Filho. He oversees telecom policy, digital inclusion, broadcasting/spectrum, postal services and the TV 3.0 initiative. In May 2026 he publicly stated he intends to remain in the ministry through the end of 2026.

Electrical engineer (Federal University of Pernambuco) and politician, national president of the Communist Party of Brazil (PCdoB). She was mayor of Olinda (2001-2008), a federal deputy and vice-governor of Pernambuco. Since 1 January 2023 she has been Brazil's Minister of Science, Technology and Innovation, overseeing R&D funding, innovation, artificial-intelligence policy and the national science, technology and innovation strategy. Despite 2025-2026 press speculation she might move to the Ministry of Women in a reshuffle, the official MCTI page (updated 28 May 2026) still lists her as minister as of mid-2026.

Retired public prosecutor, lawyer and law professor, born in Ibiúna, São Paulo, in 1962. He spent his career in the São Paulo Public Prosecutor's Office, serving twice as Attorney General of Justice (2012-2016) and as São Paulo State Secretary of Justice. He joined MDIC as Executive Secretary in January 2023, and was sworn in as Minister on 6 April 2026, succeeding Vice President Geraldo Alckmin, who left the post to run for re-election as Lula's running mate. His agenda centers on the Nova Indústria Brasil program, expanding investment and foreign trade.

Economist and academic. He holds chemical-engineering degrees from the University of São Paulo's Polytechnic School and a PhD in Economics from FGV's EPGE, where he is a professor and has coordinated WTO-chair and trade-modeling work. He has served as MDIC Secretary of Foreign Trade (SECEX) since January 2023, leading trade negotiations, the Mercosur-EU and OECD agendas, trade facilitation and export promotion, and fronting SECEX's monthly trade-balance releases and 2026 outlook statements.

Sidhu (born 1984) is a businessman and Liberal politician first elected MP for Brampton East in 2019. A University of Waterloo graduate, he ran an international-trade and customs-brokerage consulting business before politics, and served as Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers of Foreign Affairs and International Development. Sworn into PM Mark Carney's cabinet on May 13, 2025 as Minister of International Trade within Global Affairs Canada, he leads Canada's trade-diversification and export agenda, targeting a trio of trade deals in 2026. He lives in Brampton, Ontario.

LeBlanc (born December 14, 1967), a lawyer and Liberal MP for Beausejour since 2000 and son of former governor general Romeo LeBlanc, is a veteran minister who has held Fisheries, Intergovernmental Affairs, Public Safety and Finance and is often called a political 'fixer.' Since May 13, 2025 he has served as President of the King's Privy Council and Minister responsible for Canada-U.S. Trade, Intergovernmental Affairs, Internal Trade and One Canadian Economy, leading Canada's response to U.S. tariffs and the 2026 CUSMA joint review, and coordinating with provincial trade ministers.

Li Lecheng (born 27 March 1965), a mechanical-engineering graduate of Huazhong University of Science and Technology, began his career at the Shayang Machinery Factory in Hubei. He held provincial economic-planning and city-leadership posts, including director of Hubei's Development and Reform Commission, party secretary of Xiangyang, executive vice governor of Hubei, and Governor of Liaoning (2021-2025). He became MIIT party secretary in February 2025 and was appointed Minister on 30 April 2025, replacing Jin Zhuanglong. MIIT leads China's telecommunications, IT, industrial digital transformation and digital-economy policy.

Wang Wentao (born May 1964) has served as China's Minister of Commerce since December 2020. Trained in management, he built his career largely in Shanghai municipal government and later Jiangxi province, serving as mayor of Nanchang before rising to Governor of Heilongjiang province (2018-2020) and then moving to MOFCOM. As Commerce Minister he leads China's overall trade, investment and market-access policy. In 2026 he co-chaired the first China-EU Trade and Investment Consultations with EU Commissioner Maros Sefcovic and remained MOFCOM's senior figure through mid-2026.

Li Chenggang (born February 1967, Taihu County, Anhui) is a Peking University-trained lawyer with a master's in law and economics from the University of Hamburg. A career MOFCOM official, he headed the Department of Treaty and Law, served as vice mayor of Qingdao, became Assistant Minister of Commerce in 2016, and from February 2021 was China's Ambassador and Permanent Representative to the WTO in Geneva. On 16 April 2025 the State Council appointed him China International Trade Representative (full ministerial rank) and Vice Minister of Commerce, replacing Wang Shouwen, making him Beijing's chief trade negotiator.

Piyush Goyal (born 13 June 1964) is a chartered accountant and lawyer and a BJP parliamentarian, elected to the Lok Sabha from Mumbai North in 2024 after years in the Rajya Sabha from Maharashtra. He has served as Union Minister of Commerce and Industry since 2019 and leads India's overall trade policy and free-trade-agreement strategy, including the India-US bilateral trade talks, India-EU FTA, and pacts with the UK, Australia and EFTA. He has previously held the Railways, Power, and Textiles portfolios.

Rajesh Agrawal is a senior IAS officer who took charge as Commerce Secretary on 1 October 2025, having earlier served as Special Secretary and Additional Secretary in the Department of Commerce. In that role he has been India's chief negotiator for major trade deals, including the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement, the Indo-Pacific Economic Framework, the India-Australia CECA, and the ASEAN FTA review. In July 2026 he said the India-US framework agreement's groundwork was complete and both sides were ready to sign, making him India's de facto lead trade negotiator.

Budi Santoso (born 9 February 1968) is an Indonesian career civil servant and technocrat serving as Minister of Trade since October 2024 in President Prabowo Subianto's Red and White Cabinet. A long-serving Ministry of Trade official, he was Director General of Foreign Trade from 2022 to 2024 before his elevation to minister. He holds a bachelor's in communication science from Sebelas Maret University, a master's in administrative sciences from the University of Indonesia, and a doctorate from Sahid University. As minister he emphasizes expanding exports through trade agreements and manufacturing competitiveness.

Airlangga Hartarto (born 1 October 1962) is an Indonesian politician and businessman serving as Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs, a post he has held since 2019 and retained in President Prabowo Subianto's cabinet. He has acted as Indonesia's chief negotiator in trade talks with the United States, leading discussions on the reciprocal-tariff framework. Previously Minister of Industry (2016-2019) and former chairman of the Golkar Party (2017-2024), he holds a mechanical-engineering degree from Gadjah Mada University and postgraduate business degrees from Monash and Melbourne universities.

Antonio Tajani (born 1953), a founder and national coordinator of Forza Italia, is a veteran EU figure: former European Commissioner for Transport and for Industry/Entrepreneurship and President of the European Parliament (2017-2019). Since October 2022 he has been Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister in the Meloni government, where the Farnesina holds Italy's foreign-trade (commercio estero) and export-promotion competency, coordinating ITA/ICE, SACE, SIMEST and CDP. He remains active in 2026, meeting US Secretary Rubio and China's Wang Yi.

Adolfo Urso (born 12 July 1957 in Padua), an Italian politician and journalist, is a longtime figure of the Italian right (AN, then Fratelli d'Italia) and served in the Chamber of Deputies (1994-2013). He was Deputy Minister of Economic Development responsible for Foreign Trade in the second and fourth Berlusconi governments. Since 22 October 2022 he has led the renamed Ministry of Enterprises and Made in Italy, covering industrial policy, business competitiveness, the telecommunications industry and promotion of Italian production, working alongside the Foreign Ministry on exports.

Marcelo Ebrard Casaubón (born 10 October 1959) is a veteran Mexican politician (Morena). He holds a degree in international relations from El Colegio de México and studied at France's École Nationale d'Administration. He was Head of Government of Mexico City 2006-2012 and Secretary of Foreign Affairs 2018-2023 under López Obrador. After losing Morena's 2024 presidential nomination to Claudia Sheinbaum, he was appointed Secretary of Economy, taking office 1 October 2024. He leads Mexico's trade policy, including the 2026 USMCA review and US tariff negotiations.

Luis Rosendo Gutiérrez Romano is Mexico's Undersecretary for Foreign Trade, the government's lead technical trade negotiator. He holds degrees in Economics and Political Science from ITAM, a master's in Economic Development from the London School of Economics, and a PhD in Government from the University of Essex. A close associate of Marcelo Ebrard, he was appointed to the Secretaría de Economía in October 2024 and leads tariff and trade-treaty negotiations with the US and others, including the T-MEC/USMCA review and trade diversification efforts.

Andrzej Domanski (b. 1981, Krakow) is a Polish economist and Civic Coalition (KO) politician. A graduate in economics, he worked as an analyst, fund manager and investment director in financial institutions before entering the Sejm. He became Minister of Finance on 13 December 2023. After Prime Minister Tusk's July 2025 reshuffle merged the finance ministry with the dissolved Ministry of Development and Technology into a single economic super-ministry, he now heads it as Minister of Finance and Economy, directing fiscal, economic and trade-related policy. In 2026 he publicly ruled out near-term euro adoption.

Michal Baranowski is a Polish think-tank expert and policy specialist educated at Mercer University, Oxford and Maastricht. He spent nearly two decades at the German Marshall Fund of the United States, founding its Warsaw office in 2011 and later leading GMF East, specializing in transatlantic relations, trade and security. On 30 December 2024 he was appointed Undersecretary of State (deputy minister) responsible for trade. He represents Poland at the EU Foreign Affairs Council (Trade), chaired trade sessions during Poland's 2025 EU Council presidency, and in July 2026 championed the EU-India FTA as a 'huge deal' for Polish business.

Maxim Gennadyevich Reshetnikov (born 11 July 1979) has served as Minister of Economic Development since 21 January 2020 and was reappointed in May 2024. His ministry directs macroeconomic policy plus foreign economic activity, international trade negotiations and export promotion. A Perm State University economics graduate, he headed Moscow's economic-policy department (2012-2017) and governed Perm Krai (2017-2020). He remains active internationally, holding meetings with President Putin and describing Russia's economy as balanced despite global uncertainty in mid-2026.

Anton Andreyevich Alikhanov (born 17 September 1986, Sukhumi) has been Minister of Industry and Trade since 14 May 2024. Minpromtorg oversees industrial policy, domestic and foreign trade in goods, export support and import substitution. Previously governor of Kaliningrad Oblast (2016-2024), he earlier worked in the federal industry-and-trade and justice ministries. Holding degrees in finance and law, he represents Russia in bilateral trade and industrial talks, most recently a series of bilateral meetings at the INNOPROM 2026 industrial fair in July 2026.

Majid bin Abdullah Al-Qasabi has been Saudi Arabia's Minister of Commerce since May 2016 (renamed from Commerce and Investment in 2020) and remains in office in 2026, active in GCC commerce meetings. He concurrently chairs the board of the General Authority for Foreign Trade, which handles WTO representation and trade negotiations. Holding a US doctorate in industrial engineering, he previously led the King Khalid Foundation and served as acting Minister of Media (2020-2023). He is central to Vision 2030 regulatory reforms, overseeing domestic commerce, consumer protection and foreign-trade policy.

Mohammed bin Abdulaziz Al-Abduljabbar serves as Acting Governor of the General Authority for Foreign Trade (GAFT), the operational chief of Saudi Arabia's foreign-trade authority. GAFT, established 2019, represents the Kingdom at the WTO, supervises the Saudi negotiating team and leads free-trade-agreement and bilateral/regional trade negotiations; its board is chaired by the Minister of Commerce, Majid Al-Qasabi. Founding governor Abdulrahman Al-Harbi (royal order, March 2019) left in 2022 to become Ambassador to China. Al-Abduljabbar appears in an acting capacity in GAFT's own 2025-2026 communications rather than as a confirmed permanent governor.

Kim Jung-kwan (born 1968) studied economics at Seoul National University and earned a master's and doctorate from the University of Missouri. A career finance technocrat, he served at the Ministry of Economy and Finance, the Bank of Korea and the World Bank before moving to industry, including senior roles and the presidency at Doosan Enerbility. Nominated by President Lee in June 2025, he took office in July 2025 leading the ministry, renamed MOTIR after energy functions moved to the new Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment.

Yeo Han-koo is a veteran trade negotiator with nearly three decades of public service who previously served as Korea's chief trade negotiator in 2021-2022 and, before returning to government, was a senior fellow at the Peterson Institute for International Economics. He has led negotiations for RCEP and free-trade agreements with the UK, Central America, Indonesia and the Philippines. Appointed Minister for Trade in mid-2025 under President Lee, he heads MOTIR's Office of Trade Negotiations and leads tariff talks with the United States while weighing Korea's CPTPP accession.

Peter Kyle is the Labour MP for Hove and Portslade, elected in 2015. Following Labour's 2024 election victory he served as Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology (July 2024 to September 2025). In the September 2025 reshuffle he was moved to become Secretary of State for Business and Trade and President of the Board of Trade, succeeding Jonathan Reynolds, giving him lead responsibility for UK business, industrial and external trade policy, including trade agreements and export promotion. He remains in post as of July 2026.

Sir Chris Bryant is the Labour MP for Rhondda and Ogmore (previously Rhondda), an MP since 2001 and a long-serving frontbencher and former Anglican priest. Earlier in the 2024 Labour government he served as a minister for creative industries and for data protection and telecoms across DCMS and DSIT. In the September 2025 reshuffle he was appointed Minister of State for Trade Policy and Economic Security at DBT on 6 September 2025, taking charge of trade negotiations, trade agreements and economic-security policy, succeeding Douglas Alexander. He remained active in the role in 2026.

Michael Kratsios is the 13th Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy and the President's science and technology adviser, confirmed by the Senate on March 25, 2025, by a 74-25 vote. He served as U.S. Chief Technology Officer during Trump's first term and later as Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering, and was a managing director at Scale AI. He leads the administration's AI Action Plan and coordinates federal policy on artificial intelligence, quantum computing, and emerging technologies. He remains in office as of July 2026.

Arielle Roth is Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information and NTIA Administrator, the executive branch's principal adviser on telecommunications, broadband, and internet policy. The Senate confirmed her on July 23, 2025, by a 52-41 vote, and she was sworn in July 30, 2025. She previously served as telecommunications policy director for the Senate Commerce Committee's Republican staff under Senator Ted Cruz and worked at the Free State Foundation. She oversees federal spectrum management and broadband programs including BEAD, and remains in office as of July 2026.

Howard William Lutnick (born July 14, 1961) is the 41st U.S. Secretary of Commerce, confirmed by the Senate on February 18, 2025, by a 51-45 vote and sworn in that month. For decades he was chairman and CEO of Cantor Fitzgerald and BGC Group, rebuilding Cantor after it lost 658 employees on 9/11, and he co-chaired President Trump's 2024-25 transition. As Commerce Secretary he oversees trade policy, tariffs, export controls, industry promotion, and the Census, and is a leading architect of the America First trade agenda. He remains in office as of July 2026.

Jamieson Lee Greer (born August 16, 1980) is the 20th U.S. Trade Representative, confirmed by the Senate on February 27, 2025. A trade attorney and former Air Force JAG officer, he served as chief of staff to USTR Robert Lighthizer during Trump's first term, working on Section 301 China tariffs and the USMCA, and later practiced trade law at King & Spalding. As USTR he leads U.S. trade negotiations, tariff strategy, and enforcement. He announced the 2026 Trade Policy Agenda in March 2026 and testified before House Ways & Means in May 2026. He remains in office as of July 2026.
